child_tool_info.description: Build a retained nucleotide or protein BLAST database from supplied FASTA sequences.
child_tool_info.instructions: Supply one plain FASTA and choose nucleotide or protein, database format4 or5, title, identifier parsing and hash-index options explicitly. Optional taxonomy maps and masking artifacts must be supplied with their own identities; selecting this job does not generate either. Keep every produced database component, including native metadata and sidecars. A zero exit does not establish that every file was captured or that a later search used the database. A failed build can leave partial files; retain them without presenting a usable prepared database. Taxonomy assignments describe the selected inputs and do not establish gene function. Commission the selected job through launch and its configured local-compute child under the caller’s allocation. It is one native utility invocation; preparation, extraction and integrity checking are separately selected operations. The infrastructure does not choose follow-up work. Retain original inputs, output files and diagnostic streams. Results acquisition uses the deterministic typed utility records and returns only the parent’s requested fields. These are supporting operations without an independent annotation-confidence score. Keep database-scale work off this local resource; remote execution requires its own actually configured resource binding.
child_tool_info.name: native.makeblastdb.create_sequence_database

child_tool_info.description: Retrieve explicitly selected sequences or ranges from a supplied prepared BLAST database.
child_tool_info.instructions: Select an already prepared database and an explicit list of sequence identifiers. This binding does not select a default database or retrieve all entries. Duplicate requests remain distinct. Native identifier, accession, OID and full sequence length accompany the returned sequence. A requested range uses one-based inclusive endpoints; retained normalized coordinates use zero-based half-open endpoints. The returned fragment length is distinct from the full sequence length. Preserve strand, missing identifiers and unassociated rows. Do not join records by output position or choose the first duplicate accession. get_dups and target_only are mutually exclusive native options. Commission the selected job through launch and its configured local-compute child under the caller’s allocation. It is one native utility invocation; preparation, extraction and integrity checking are separately selected operations. The infrastructure does not choose follow-up work. Retain original inputs, output files and diagnostic streams. Results acquisition uses the deterministic typed utility records and returns only the parent’s requested fields. These are supporting operations without an independent annotation-confidence score. Keep database-scale work off this local resource; remote execution requires its own actually configured resource binding.
